title: Needs you
how: Only what is open for you, oldest first. Each item says what to do, links everything it needs, and gives my recommendation. It leaves this page once you have answered it here or done it.
Pick an answer under each item; a note is optional.
foot: One page, one link, kept current (his order of 2 November). The same list is kept as plain data beside it (items.json) for the advisor's checker.

sections.name: Confirm your chat answers of 08:13? (1) No paste into CLAUDE.md: the five changes go into the rulings instead, and the rest of the records change is done as proposed. (2) The connectors stay as they are. (3) The AI-video motion experiment runs now, with video made only on your PC: no outside service, no payment; free stock clips from Pexels and Pixabay, whose licences allow commercial use and changes but are not yet on the allowed list, are added to it for motion reference only and serve as the real-footage control. You never film or perform anything.
sections.recommendation: Yes: it is what you said in the chat, written down once so every session works from it. HY-Motion is left out: it needs far more video memory than your card has. No web link: the answer is this page.

sections.name: Install Epic's free motion-capture plugin (needs your sign-in): open the link, sign in, press 'Add to My Library'; then in the Epic Games Launcher go to Unreal Engine, Library, Fab Library, find 'MetaHuman Animator Markerless Motion Capture Plugin', press 'Install to Engine' and pick 5.8. If Windows asks about an unsigned file, allow it.

links.label: The plugin on Fab (Epic Games, free)

sections.recommendation: Done: the motion experiment's capture half needs it, and it is Epic's own, free, under the Fab licence the list allows. About three minutes of your time.

sections.name: Room for the motion experiment: the video program and its model need about 25 GB, and drive F is at its 20 GB floor with every large folder on it protected. May they go on drive C (in C:\LedgerTools, as the live voice already is) for this week's experiment, removed once it is judged?
sections.recommendation: Yes, on C: C keeps about 79 GB above its 40 GB floor after it, and nothing of yours on F is touched. No web link: the answer is this page.
